deities: Shiva (presiding deity, worshipped as Umamaheswara with Goddess Uma)
festivals: Revathi Pattathanam (7-day festival in October-November; annual assembly of scholars and cultural events, traditionally started by the Zamorins)
Annual temple festival in the Malayalam month of Medam (flag hoisting in the Shiva and Krishna temples, concluding with Arattu)

history.dynasty: Zamorin (Samoothiri) of Calicut; founded by Swami Thirumulpad
history.summary: Tali Mahakshetram, dedicated to Shiva, stands at Palayam in the heart of Kozhikode and was the family temple of the Zamorins who ruled Calicut. It was built in the 14th century by Swami Thirumulpad, the Zamorin, within his palace complex, and the founding and prosperity of Kozhikode city are closely linked with the sanctity of this temple (the area around it was once called Kovilkota). Legend holds that the Jyotirlingam in the sanctum sanctorum was installed by Parasurama towards the end of the Dwapara Yuga; the deity is worshipped in the Umamaheswara posture, with Shiva and Goddess Uma as one. Note that the 'jyotirlingam' here means a self-manifested, deeply sacred lingam in local tradition, not one of the twelve Dwadasa Jyotirlingas. The temple was nearly destroyed during Tipu Sultan's invasion of Kozhikode in the 18th century and was renovated in 1964. Built in classic Kerala style, the two-storied sanctum sanctorum is shaped like a chariot and adorned with murals and granite sculptures of Shiva's retinue. The temple is now under the Malabar Devaswom Board, with the Zamorin continuing as the managing trustee, and it has long been a centre of scholarship as the venue of the Revathi Pattathanam assembly of philosophers and poets.

name: Tali Mahakshetram
town_description: Kozhikode (formerly Calicut) is a major port city on Kerala's Malabar Coast and was the capital of the Zamorin kingdom, famed as the historic hub of the spice trade with Arab and European merchants. Vasco da Gama first landed in India at nearby Kappad in 1498. The city blends colonial-era history with modern Malabar culture, and the Tali Mahakshetram sits at its very heart near the Palayam market, about 1 km from the railway station.

travel.airport: Calicut International Airport (approx. 23-27 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Kozhikode Railway Station (approx. 1-2 km); autos and local buses readily available.
travel.road: Centrally located at Tali Road, Palayam, in the heart of Kozhikode city, near the Palayam market; easily reached by city buses, auto-rickshaws and taxis.

visitor_information.best_time: October to May, when Kerala's weather is most pleasant. Maha Shivaratri and the Revathi Pattathanam (October-November) are the most vibrant times to visit.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 4:30 AM to 11:00 AM; evening 5:00 PM to 8:30 PM (verify - one travel guide lists 5:00 AM to 12:00 noon and 4:00 PM to 9:00 PM instead). Strict traditional dress code: men must wear veshti/mundu without a shirt (available for rent at the temple counter); jeans and western attire are not permitted inside. Entry for general darshan is free.
